message.content:
In Christian theology, the focus is generally on the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central figure of faith. Many Christians regard Jesus as the fulfillment of Old‑Testament prophecy and the ultimate revelation of God’s plan for humanity.  

At the same time, the Old Testament contains many prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—whose writings and actions are highly respected and form an essential part of the biblical canon. These prophets are seen as important for understanding the context and continuity of the Christian narrative.

Different Christian traditions may emphasize various prophets or aspects of prophetic ministry, but overall, Jesus is typically viewed as the pivotal figure around whom Christian belief revolves.
